newsitem.title: CANADA: Bema, Arizona up on Chile results.
newsitem.headline: Bema, Arizona up on Chile results.

text.p: Shares in two Canadian exploration companies climbed Thursday after they released new estimates for their copper and gold prospect in Chile that suggested it could be among the richest in Latin America.
The shares of Bema Gold Corp and Arizona Star Resource Corp managed to escape a pall cast on the Canadian mineral exploration sector by doubts about Bre-X Minerals Ltd's Busang discovery.
Bema was up 0.75 to 11.05 in Toronto while Arizona Star gained 0.90 to 11.90 on the Vancouver exchange.

In a release Wednesday, Bema and Arizona Star said an "independently calculated in situ resource estimate" for the Cerro Casale deposit in in Chile projected it contains 24.8 million ounces of gold and 6.4 billion pounds of copper.
The estimates were based on a gold cut-off grade of 0.4 grams a tonne. The companies presented three estimates using different cut-off grades.

Two lower resource estimates were based on cut-off grades of 0.5 and 0.55 grams a tonne of gold. These yielded estimates of 20.6 million ounces of gold and 5.0 billion pounds of copper and 18.7 million ounces of gold and 4.4 billion pounds of copper.
The estimates were prepared by California consultants Mineral Resources Development Inc and were based on 261 drill holes.

CIBC Wood Gundy analyst Bill Belovay said investors remained wary because of Bre-X's stock collapse, but were reassured because outside consultants had been involved at Cerro Casale from the initial stages. He set a one-year price target for Bema of 16.
Gordon Capital analyst Stephen Walker said the favorable results boosted Bema and Arizona Star, but the stocks were retracing ground lost in the recent market downturn.
"They are just getting back to where they were pre-Bre-X...There is still a lot of concern about Bre-X," he said.
He expected the companies to bring in a senior mining company to help develop the property and set price targets of 14.60 for Bema and 18 for Arizona Star shares.

Bema said it believes the deposit "will be a world class open-pit copper gold mine." Company officials were not available for further comment. Traders have speculated that Bema might be willing to do a joint venture deal. The company has said in the past its first priority was to obtain enough data to understand the property and did not rule out developing the deposit itself.
